citeAs: Langlais, Pierre-Carl, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Amett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, and Ivan P. Yamshchikov. (2025). Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training. arXiv.
creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Amett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov (PleIAs)
description: Common Corpus is a large open dataset for language model pre-training assembled from uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data. It aggregates six collections—Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Code, Open Web, and Open Semantic—covering multilingual text and code, with about 2 trillion tokens and per-document metadata such as license and language.
name: Common Corpus
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly notes that web data often contain harmful and biased content, including sexual content, hate speech, and racial and gender biases, and that historical public-domain texts may contain outdated harmful language about ethnic groups, women, violence, and other themes. To mitigate these biases, the creators apply toxicity filtering and synthetic rewriting, avoid machine translation for multilingual content, and remove personally identifiable information.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled since 2024 by aggregating six collections: Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Code, Open Web, and Open Semantic. Data were collected from public-domain and permissively licensed sources including APIs, standard retrieval methods, OpenAlex, Hugging Face releases, GitHub-linked code corpora, Wikimedia projects, YouTube transcripts, StackExchange, and Wikidata adapted to text.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data include scientific papers and theses, legal and administrative documents, financial PDFs, cultural heritage books and newspapers, code repositories from the Stack v1/v2, Wikimedia rendered HTML dumps, YouTube audio transcripts, StackExchange posts, and Wikidata RDF triples converted into textual sequences.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The collection effort has been ongoing since 2024, with Common Corpus first published in March 2024 and the version described in the paper released in February 2025.
rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Web API, Software Collection, Web Scraping, User-generated content data, Others
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not cover the full range of available open data, has shallow coverage for low-resource languages, and its 2 trillion tokens are more suitable for pre-training limited-size models than larger ones. It does not contain data for instruction-tuning or specialized tasks, and the curation methods such as OCR correction, toxicity detection, and PII removal are not perfectly accurate.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-collection manipulations include OCR correction with OCRonos, rewriting highly deteriorated OCR text, replacing personally identifiable information with fictitious but realistic values, removing or synthetically rewriting documents containing harmful language, converting Wikidata triples into text sequences, and deriving a more intensively filtered refined version of about 1 trillion tokens for later training.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The paper describes segmentation, filtering, rights verification, OCR quality detection, OCR correction, PII replacement, toxicity filtering, and format-specific cleaning. Examples include parsing Wikimedia rendered HTML, converting Wikidata triples into natural-language-like sequences, removing undesired file types in code data, normalizing line breaks, filtering licenses, and attaching metadata such as source URL, license, language, and collection.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus is described as an evolving resource rather than a fixed dataset, with official releases expanding it over time and HuggingFace ensuring proper archiving of past versions for reproducibility.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is presented as infrastructure for open science and legally compliant LLM development, aiming to reduce reliance on copyrighted or restricted training data. The paper discusses positive impact for reproducible and auditable open models, while also addressing ethical risks such as harmful language, privacy, and regulatory compliance through toxicity filtering and PII handling.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses include pre-training fully open and auditable LLMs, training multilingual and code models, multimodal document processing, creative writing models, historical language models, legal and administrative language models, retrieval-augmented generation models, and building derivative datasets, benchmarks, classifiers, and speech or multimodal resources.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Segmentext for text segmentation; OCRoscope based on cld2 for OCR quality detection; OCRerrcr, a DeBERTa-v2-style model, for OCR error detection; OCRonos based on Llama 3 8B for OCR correction; Microsoft Presidio for PII detection; fastText language identification; and Celadon, a DeBERTa-v3-small multilingual toxicity classifier, for harmful-content detection.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper states that personally identifiable information (PII) is present in source data and is removed. They identify and replace PII using Microsoft Presidio and custom regular expressions, replacing detected PII with fictitious but realistic values.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: paper describes curation and filtering but not a per-item human annotation count for Common Corpus itself
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: no demographics of annotators or curators are provided
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: no human annotation platform for the dataset itself is described
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: paper discusses data curation and model-based filtering, not a human labeling protocol for Common Corpus items
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: no inter-annotator agreement or annotation quality analysis for Common Corpus labels is reported
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: paper does not explicitly discuss missing data or unavailable observations in the dataset
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: no missing-value imputation or fill-in protocol is described; replacements discussed are for PII and OCR/toxicity rewriting rather than missing data
null_reasons.license: paper states documents carry varying licenses and gives examples, but does not state a single overall dataset license for Common Corpus
